stories.research_notes:
Here is a factual research note on *“Community efforts preserve Lantern Bay Park trees”*, based on municipal documents and independent reporting.

---

## What Happened

- On **November 17, 2026**, the Dana Point City Council adopted the recommendation from the Lantern Bay Park subcommittee to *preserve all existing trees* in Lantern Bay Park. The resolution specifies: “with no trees designated for removal under Condition 18 of Planning Commission Resolution No. 25-09-22-32.” ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))

- Alongside preserving the trees, the Council took several related actions:

  1. **Ocean Cliffs at Dana Point** (a JW Marriott resort) was relieved of its financial obligation under *Condition 20* of that same Planning Commission resolution, *but* maintained its duties under *Conditions 15 and 16* to restore areas disturbed by the waterline installation and the area leading up to the resort’s pool wall. ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))

  2. The Council decided that any future improvements to Lantern Bay Park should be placed on the **City’s Capital Improvement Program** (CIP) and funded by the City, rather than by the resort. ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))

  3. The City Council also **sunset** (ended) the Lantern Bay Park Subcommittee. ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))

---

## Background / Context

- The controversy dates back to a proposal from Marriott (Ocean Cliffs) tied to a water-line installation in the park: The resort proposed to fund and build significant park renovations in exchange for that right-of-entry, including a botanical garden, amphitheater improvements, walkways, and removal of two stands of mature pine trees (Torrey pines and Stone pines). ([ocdevelopment.net](https://ocdevelopment.net/article/dana-point-council-seeks-tree-preservation-in-lantern-bay-park-renovation-plans-ih07p?utm_source=openai))

- On **October 6, 2026**, the City Council voted 3-2 in favor of advancing the conceptual design and agreement—with tree removal under Condition 18 included. However, because of strong public opposition, the Council also formed a *subcommittee* (Mayor Pro Tem Frost and Council Member Pagano) to work with the resort and community to revise the plan. ([mytownview.com](https://mytownview.com/california/orange/dana-point/meetings/7763-city-council-2026-10-06?utm_source=openai))

- Community mobilization included more than **3,000 petition signatures**, over 120 public comments, rallies, and a survey of 75 park users (45 residents) which found that more than half wanted to keep existing landscaping and add shade/seating, while only a few favored removing trees to open up harbor views. ([siliconvalleymovingpost.com](https://siliconvalleymovingpost.com/residents-lobby-for-preservation-of-pine-trees-in-dana-points-lantern-bay-park/?utm_source=openai))

---

## Outcome vs. Plan

- **Completed outcome (as of Nov 17, 2026):** The Council officially resolved to preserve *all existing trees* in the park (i.e. none to be removed under the relevant resolution’s tree-removal condition). Improvements will only proceed under City funding through its CIP. Ocean Cliffs is freed from funding obligations for park improvements tied to the earlier agreement under Condition 20, except for restoring disturbed areas. ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))

- **What was proposed but not approved / what was altered:**
  
  - Original plans (as of October 6) that included removal of mature pine stands (around 70 trees) have been superseded by the subcommittee recommendation for zero tree removal. ([ocdevelopment.net](https://ocdevelopment.net/article/dana-point-council-seeks-tree-preservation-in-lantern-bay-park-renovation-plans-ih07p?utm_source=openai))

  - The proposal for resort-funded park renovations has been changed so that future improvements will be city-funded via the CIP, rather than under the resort’s obligations. ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))

---

## Sources

**Primary Sources:**

- City of Dana Point City Council Agenda, *Item #13: Lantern Bay Park Subcommittee Recommendation*, November 17, 2026. ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/a111726_linked.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- Public staff report & minutes from the November 17 meeting (including Condition 18 and 20 references). ([danapoint.org](https://www.danapoint.org/files/assets/city/v/1/city-council/documents/meetings-agendas-and-minutes/2026/11172026/13.-lantern-bay-park.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**Independent Sources:**

- San Clemente Source: *“Dana Point Residents Rally, Council Moves to Save Lantern Bay Park Trees”* (Oct 22, 2026). ([sanclementesource.com](https://sanclementesource.com/article/dana-point-residents-rally-council-moves-to-save-lantern-bay-park-trees-uhtxr?utm_source=openai))  
- Orange County Register: *“Residents lobby for preservation of pine trees in Dana Point’s Lantern Bay Park”* (Oct 16, 2026). ([siliconvalleymovingpost.com](https://siliconvalleymovingpost.com/residents-lobby-for-preservation-of-pine-trees-in-dana-points-lantern-bay-park/?utm_source=openai))

stories.verified_headline: Dana Point Council Preserves Trees in Lantern Bay Park
stories.verified_summary: On November 17, 2026, the Dana Point City Council resolved to preserve all existing trees in Lantern Bay Park, responding to strong community opposition against proposed tree removals. This decision followed significant public mobilization, including over 3,000 petition signatures.
stories.verification_note: The evidence shows a completed outcome where the City Council officially preserved all trees, backed by multiple independent sources detailing community efforts and council actions.
